ambiguities_or_notes: Every source block (40) has a matching target block, with page markers, numbering, quotation structure, and italics preserved.

Website Circle of Reading paragraphs served as the first draft; each was re-read against the Russian and revised where it drifted (omissions, additions, generic he/his, terminology, attribution form).

The source cites the psalm in the Russian Synodal numbering as «Пс. 89, ст. 10» (Ps. 89, v. 10); the reference is given as Psalm 90:10, its number in English Bibles, and the verse is translated from Tolstoy's Russian («труд и болезнь», trud i bolezn', 'labor and sickness'), not from the KJV. «Безумец» / «безумный» (bezumets / bezumnyy, 'fool, madman') is 'fool' in the Buddhist sayings and in the Luke parable alike; the attribution keeps «бен» as 'ben' (Said ben Hamed).
